title: Capacity Recapture & Price Sensitivity Model (Q1 2027)
summary: Working model to test a capacity recapture program (reallocating reserved GPU hours, tightening burst buffers, and modest price increases) and the downstream impact on hiring needs, monthly burn, and per-token unit economics under three scenarios (Base / Aggressive recapture / Conservative).
assumptions:
- Planning window: Q1 2027 (Jan–Mar).
- Current committed reserved capacity cost (GPU fleet + infra amortization): $1.8M / month.
- Burst capacity (on-demand) delta to reserved: 2.2x cost per token.
- Average fully-burdened engineer salary: $220k/year (burden factor 1.35 -> monthly cost $24,833).
- Average support rep salary: $110k/year (burden factor 1.25 -> monthly cost $9,104).
- Expected token growth (organic) 18% q/q if no price change.
- Price elasticity assumptions: small price lift (5%) -> -6% demand; medium lift (10%) -> -13% demand.
- Quantization/optimizer savings can recapture ~12% of GPU spend without user-visible changes (conservative bound 8%, optimistic 15%).

scenarios:
Base: No price change, attempt 8% platform optimization recapture + small scheduling improvements.
Aggressive Recapture: 15% infra recapture via quantization + batching + policy shift; simultaneously introduce targeted 5% price lift for high-value customers.
Conservative Recapture: Only 5% infra wins; still test 5% price lift but expect only -2% demand drop due to segmentation and credits.
key_insights:
- Biggest levers: infra recapture (kernel optimizations + quantization) and marginal price increases targeted at low-elasticity segments.
- At 15% infra recapture the monthly infra spend improvement (~$296k) covers ~85% of planned incremental HC burn in the Aggressive case.
- 5% price lift is net-positive under aggressive recapture. Under conservative recapture, margin compression risk increases if we still pursue the same hiring plan.
- Sensitivity is non-linear: a further 3% demand drop amplifies margin loss more than proportional because burst/on-demand costs step up sharply at thresholds.
open_questions:
- Risk: If competitors match price, will demand elasticity worsen? Need scenario with competitor price parity.
- Timing: how fast can quantization/compile kernel wins be deployed operationally (engineer ETA 6–10 weeks)?
- Customer segmentation: which customers get price lift vs grandfathered credits? Need Sales/CS decision matrix.
- Accounting: treatment of infra savings vs one-time implementation cost (capital vs expense).

quick_calcs_and_formulas:
- Monthly fully-burdened cost per engineer = salary * burden / 12. Example: 220,000 * 1.35 / 12 = 24,833.
- Infra recapture $ = ReservedGPUCost * recapture_pct.
- New monthly margin = Revenue - (InfraPostRecapture + IncrementalHCBurn).
- Elastic demand after price lift = baseline_demand * (1 - elasticity * price_lift).
